# E035 -- The New School Brand Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Company:** The New School
- **Industry:** Education
- **Year:** 2015
- **Source file:** newschool-2015-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 55
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "The New School Brand Guidelines -- Version 1.0," updated March 30, 2015
- Five sections: Introduction, Brand Elements, Brand Logo, Print Identity Application, Digital Identity Application
- No brand mission, vision, or positioning content observed in sampled pages -- focused on visual identity execution

## Logo
- Brand Logo has its own dedicated section (Section 3) -- not covered in sampled pages
- Identity associated with Parsons School of Design (Parsons Red color named after it)

## Typography
- Dedicated typography section (Section 2:2-2:5)
- Primary typeface: "Neue" type family -- custom/proprietary font
- "Neue Random" font: uses OpenType algorithm that cycles through characters of various widths as you type
  - Requires enabling: Kerning, Ligatures, Contextual Alternates
  - Installation instructions for Mac (Microsoft Word, PowerPoint) and PC
  - Contextual Alternates and Ligatures on by default in PowerPoint; must be manually enabled in Word
- Typography Violations section (2:4) -- indicates strict typographic rules
- The variable-width cycling behavior creates a distinctive, dynamic visual identity

## Color
- Three core colors:
  - Pantone Parsons Red: Rubine Red(51) + Yellow 012(49) / CMYK C5-M98-Y100-K0 / RGB 232-46-33 / HEX #E82E21
  - Black: CMYK 0-0-0-100 / RGB 0-0-0 / HEX #000000
  - White: CMYK 0-0-0-0 / RGB 255-255-255 / HEX #FFFFFF
- Core palette should never be dominated or substituted
- Pantone color matching disclaimer included

- Not covered in sampled pages

## Applications
- Section 4: Print Identity Application
- Section 5: Digital Identity Application
- Separate print and digital application sections suggest thorough implementation guidance

## Tone of Voice
- Not addressed in this document

## Outliers
- "Neue Random" algorithmic font is highly distinctive -- an OpenType feature that randomizes character widths creates a unique, ever-changing typographic identity
- Named after Parsons School of Design ("Parsons Red") -- the color system carries institutional heritage
- Extremely minimal core palette (only red, black, white) -- bold constraint for an educational institution
- Installation troubleshooting for the custom font included -- practical implementation focus
- Identity system designed by Pentagram (based on the well-known 2011 rebrand)

## Quality Score
- **Score: 3/5** -- Well-organized identity guide with strong typographic identity (the Neue Random font is genuinely innovative), precise color specifications, and practical implementation guidance including font installation instructions. However, lacks brand strategy, tone of voice, photography, and broader brand narrative. The three-color constraint and algorithmic typography are distinctive design decisions that compensate for the limited scope.
